## Figure 3.3: Three Years of the Creditor Data-Sharing Exercise
Type: combined bar-and-line chart (bars plus two line series, dual y-axes)

- **Time span / categories on x-axis:** End-2021, End-2023, End-2024
- **Left y-axis:** **US$ (billions)**, range **0 to 70**
- **Right y-axis:** **Loans and tranches**, range **0 to 5,000**
- **Legend / series:**
  - **Debt outstanding reported** (dark blue bars)
  - **Loans and tranches reported** (light blue line with markers)
  - **Loans matched** (orange line with markers)

### Values shown
| Period | Debt outstanding reported (US$ billions) | Loans and tranches reported | Loans matched |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| End-2021 | 62.9 | 3,655 | 2,904 |
| End-2023 | 61.8 | 4,692 | 3,437 |
| End-2024 | 63.4 | 4,875 | 3,762 |

### Callouts printed above the chart
- **18 Participating creditors**  
  **▲ from 17 in 2023**
- **4,875 Loans reported**  
  **▲ 33% from 3,655 in 2021**
- **$63.4 billion Debt reported**  
  **▲ 3% from $61.8 billion in 2023**

### Visual comparisons and trends
- **Debt outstanding reported** is highest in **End-2024 (63.4)**, slightly below that in **End-2021 (62.9)**, and lowest in **End-2023 (61.8)**.
- **Loans and tranches reported** rise steadily: **3,655 → 4,692 → 4,875**.
- **Loans matched** also rise steadily: **2,904 → 3,437 → 3,762**.
- In every year, **loans and tranches reported exceed loans matched**.
- The increase from **2023 to 2024** is small for debt outstanding reported (**61.8 to 63.4**) but positive.
- The largest absolute increase among the count series is in **loans and tranches reported** from **End-2021 to End-2023**.

**Sources:** Original calculations based on Group of Seven and Paris Club creditor files; World Bank Group Debtor Reporting System.

## Figure 3.4: Asymmetries Between Creditor and Borrower Claims on Debt Outstanding Position at End-2024
Type: scatter plot

- **x-axis:** **Total reported by borrowers (US$, million)**
- **y-axis:** **Total reported by creditors (US$, million)**
- **Axis ranges:** both axes run from **10** to **100,000**
- **Scale:** both axes are **logarithmic**
- **Reference line:** dotted 45-degree line indicating equality between borrower- and creditor-reported totals
- **Coverage noted:** selected International Development Association debtors and Group of Seven/Paris Club creditors

### Plotted points
No printed point labels are shown. Approximate coordinates from point positions:

| Point | Total reported by borrowers (US$, million) | Total reported by creditors (US$, million) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | ≈50 | ≈160 |
| 2 | ≈65 | ≈1,000 |
| 3 | ≈70 | ≈110 |
| 4 | ≈78 | ≈45 |
| 5 | ≈150 | ≈430 |
| 6 | ≈250 | ≈190 |
| 7 | ≈400 | ≈480 |
| 8 | ≈480 | ≈520 |
| 9 | ≈720 | ≈110 |
| 10 | ≈1,050 | ≈2,700 |
| 11 | ≈1,400 | ≈720 |
| 12 | ≈1,900 | ≈1,000 |
| 13 | ≈2,400 | ≈2,400 |
| 14 | ≈4,200 | ≈540 |
| 15 | ≈4,600 | ≈4,300 |
| 16 | ≈6,200 | ≈950 |
| 17 | ≈13,000 | ≈14,500 |
| 18 | ≈32,000 | ≈31,000 |

### Visual comparisons and patterns
- Most observations lie **near** the 45-degree line, but several show substantial asymmetries.
- The **largest borrower-reported value** is approximately **32,000**, with creditor-reported value approximately **31,000**; this point lies very close to parity.
- Another high-value point is around **13,000 borrower / 14,500 creditor**, slightly **above** the parity line.
- The **largest creditor-over-borrower asymmetry** appears around **65 borrower / 1,000 creditor**, well **above** the line.
- The **largest borrower-over-creditor asymmetries** include points around:
  - **≈4,200 borrower / ≈540 creditor**
  - **≈6,200 borrower / ≈950 creditor**
  - **≈720 borrower / ≈110 creditor**
- Several mid-range points lie close to parity, including roughly:
  - **≈2,400 / ≈2,400**
  - **≈32,000 / ≈31,000**
  - **≈13,000 / ≈14,500**
- There are **no negative values**; all values are positive by construction of the logarithmic axes.

**Sources:** Original calculations based on Group of Seven and Paris Club creditor files; World Bank Group Debtor Reporting System.  
**Note:** Data for selected International Development Association debtors and Group of Seven/Paris Club creditors. Both axes are on a logarithmic scale.
